senses.gloss: In a relaxed, offhand way, without much thought or attention.
examples: He *casually* mentioned that he'd quit his job.
She leaned *casually* against the wall.
He glanced *casually* at the clock, trying not to look nervous.

senses.gloss: In an informal way, especially about clothes.
examples: Most people at the office dress *casually* on Fridays.
The guests were *casually* dressed in jeans and T-shirts.

position: end — also before an adjective (*catastrophically bad*)

senses.gloss: In a way that causes or amounts to a disaster.
examples: The bridge failed *catastrophically* during the storm.
The plan went *catastrophically* wrong.
A *catastrophically* bad harvest left thousands of families hungry.

position: mid — before verbs like *deny*, *reject*, *refuse*; also end
modifies: verbs of saying, denying and refusing

senses.gloss: Absolutely and without any doubt or exception.
examples: The senator *categorically* denied the report.
We *categorically* reject any form of violence.
I can tell you *categorically* that no one was hurt.

contrast: Do not confuse with *casually* (небрежно) — the same letters in a different order. *Causally related* means one thing causes the other; *casually related* is a misprint.

senses.gloss: As cause and effect.
examples: The two events are not *causally* related.
Smoking is *causally* linked to lung cancer.
The study could not show that the drug and the side effects were *causally* connected.

senses.gloss: In a bitterly sarcastic, critical way.
examples: "Thanks for nothing," she said *caustically*.
He wrote *caustically* about the new mayor.
The critic *caustically* dismissed the movie as a two-hour commercial.

senses.gloss: Carefully, so as to avoid risk or mistakes.
examples: She stepped *cautiously* onto the ice.
Doctors are *cautiously* optimistic about his recovery.
Drive *cautiously* — the roads are still wet.

senses.gloss: In an offhand, dismissive way that ignores serious concerns or other people's feelings.
examples: The company treated its customers' complaints *cavalierly*.
He *cavalierly* brushed aside the safety warnings.
Our personal data was handled rather *cavalierly*.

senses.gloss: Without stopping, for a long time.
examples: The rain fell *ceaselessly* for three days.
She worked *ceaselessly* to get her brother released.
The waves beat *ceaselessly* against the rocks.

position: before its word — before a participle (*centrally located*); also end

senses.gloss: In or near the center of a place.
examples: The hotel is *centrally* located, close to all the museums.
We need an office that is *more centrally* placed.

senses.gloss: From one central place or authority rather than locally.
examples: The heating in the building is controlled *centrally*.
The Soviet economy was *centrally* planned.

position: before its word — before a participle; also end

senses.gloss: As part of a formal ceremony or ritual.
examples: The new bridge was *ceremonially* opened by the governor.
Every evening the flag is *ceremonially* lowered.
The keys to the city were *ceremonially* handed to the astronauts.

senses.gloss: In a completely disorganized, confused way.
examples: Kids ran *chaotically* around the playground.
The evacuation was handled *chaotically*.
Papers were piled *chaotically* on every desk.

position: front — also before an adjective (*characteristically modest*)
modifies: a whole clause, adjectives, and verbs

senses.gloss: In a way that is typical of a particular person or thing.
examples: *Characteristically*, she arrived early and stayed late.
He was *characteristically* modest about his success.
The speech was *characteristically* short and blunt.

position: end — also front in *to put it charitably*
modifies: verbs of judging, describing and treating

senses.gloss: In a kind, generous way that judges others favorably.
examples: To put it *charitably*, the movie was not his best work.
She *charitably* assumed he had simply forgotten.
Try to view their mistakes a little *more charitably*.

position: before its word — before an adjective; also end

senses.gloss: In a pleasant, attractive way.
examples: The inn is *charmingly* old-fashioned.
He smiled *charmingly* at the waitress.
The story is simple but *charmingly* told.

position: end — also before a participle (*cheaply made*)
contrast: Informal American English also uses the flat adverb *cheap* after verbs of buying and selling (*I got it cheap*). Before a participle only *cheaply* works: *cheaply made*, not *cheap made*.

senses.gloss: For little money; at a low cost, often with low quality.
examples: You can eat *cheaply* in this part of town.
The shelves were *cheaply* made and fell apart in a year.
We found a way to do the job *more cheaply*.

senses.gloss: In a happy, good-humored way; willingly.
examples: She *cheerfully* agreed to help us move.
He whistled *cheerfully* as he worked.
The kids waved *cheerfully* from the school bus.

senses.gloss: In a bright, friendly, cheerful way.
examples: "Good morning!" he called *cheerily*.
A fire crackled *cheerily* in the fireplace.
She waved *cheerily* and drove off.

position: before its word — before a participle (*chemically treated*); also end or front
modifies: participles, adjectives, verbs, and a whole clause

senses.gloss: By means of chemistry or chemicals; in terms of chemistry.
examples: The wood has been *chemically* treated to resist rot.
Gold does not react *chemically* with air.
*Chemically*, water is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

contrast: *Childishly* is a criticism — immature, silly. Russian *по-детски* can also be warm (*по-детски искренне*); for that use *childlike* (*with childlike wonder*), which has no common adverb.

senses.gloss: In a silly, immature way, like a child.
examples: Stop behaving so *childishly*.
He *childishly* refused to speak to her for a week.
She was *childishly* excited about the snow.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle

senses.gloss: Over a long time or again and again, as a lasting condition or habit.
examples: Her mother is *chronically* ill.
He is *chronically* late for meetings.
Schools in the county have been *chronically* underfunded for years.

senses.gloss: In the order in which things happened.
examples: The photos are arranged *chronologically*.
Let's go through the events *chronologically*.
*Chronologically*, the second book comes before the first.

position: end — before *liable* in the legal sense
modifies: verbs; *liable* and *responsible* in the legal sense

senses.gloss: Politely, in a correct but not especially friendly way.
examples: Even though they disagreed, they spoke to each other *civilly*.
Please try to treat each other *civilly*.

senses.gloss: Under civil law rather than criminal law.
examples: The company could be held *civilly* liable for the damage.
He was never charged with a crime, but the family sued him *civilly*.

position: before its word — before a participle or adjective

senses.gloss: In the classical or traditional style; in a way that is a perfect typical example.
examples: She is a *classically* trained pianist.
The building is *classically* proportioned, with tall white columns.
It's a *classically* American story of a poor kid who made it big.

senses.gloss: In a smart, inventive or skillful way.
examples: The thief *cleverly* disguised himself as a security guard.
The puzzle is *cleverly* designed.
The ad was funny and *cleverly* written.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; end in the 'coldly' sense
modifies: adjectives and participles (*clinically depressed*, *clinically proven*), and verbs

senses.gloss: In medical terms; as shown by doctors' examination or medical tests.
examples: He was diagnosed as *clinically* depressed.
The cream is *clinically* proven to reduce wrinkles.
The patient was declared *clinically* dead.

senses.gloss: In a cold, detached way, without emotion.
examples: She described the accident almost *clinically*.
The room was *clinically* white and bare.

position: before its word — before an adjective

senses.gloss: Too sweet or sentimental, in an unpleasant way.
examples: The frosting was *cloyingly* sweet.
The movie ends on a *cloyingly* sentimental note.
Her voice was *cloyingly* polite.

senses.gloss: In an awkward, careless or unskillful way.
examples: He *clumsily* knocked over his glass.
The letter was *clumsily* written.
She moved *clumsily* in the heavy boots.

position: end — also before a participle (*coarsely ground*)
contrast: Russian *грубо* covers both *coarsely* and *roughly*. About people, *coarsely* means vulgar or crude; for violent or rough treatment use *roughly*. In a recipe, *coarsely chopped* and *roughly chopped* mean the same.

senses.gloss: In large or rough pieces, not finely.
examples: Chop the onions *coarsely*.
Season with salt and *coarsely* ground black pepper.

senses.gloss: In a rude, vulgar way.
examples: He laughed *coarsely* at his own joke.
The men were joking *coarsely* at the bar.

position: before its word — before an adjective; also front

senses.gloss: In terms of thinking, learning and memory.
examples: Older adults who stay *cognitively* active tend to remember more.
The test shows how *cognitively* flexible a child is.
*Cognitively*, the task is very demanding.

modifies: verbs of speaking, thinking and organizing

senses.gloss: In a clear, logical way that is easy to follow.
examples: He was too upset to speak *coherently*.
She argued her case *coherently* and calmly.
The report needs to be organized *more coherently*.

position: front — also mid, set off by commas

senses.gloss: By chance, as a coincidence.
examples: *Coincidentally*, we were born on the same day.
The meeting was, *coincidentally*, on my birthday.
Not *coincidentally*, prices went up right after the merger.

contrast: *Coldly* is only about an unfriendly manner. Russian *холодно* also describes weather, and there English uses the adjective: *It's cold outside*, never *It's coldly*.

senses.gloss: In an unfriendly way, without warmth or emotion.
examples: She looked at him *coldly* and said nothing.
"I have nothing to say to you," he replied *coldly*.
Our offer was received *coldly*.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective in *a collect call*
contrast: The same spelling is the ordinary verb *collect* (*collect stamps*). As an adverb it appears only in *call collect*, and the noun phrase is *a collect call*. Mostly American, and less common since cell phones.

senses.gloss: With the person who receives the phone call paying for it.
examples: I called my parents *collect* from the bus station.
Can I call *collect* from this phone?
He had no money, so he phoned home *collect*.

modifies: verbs, participles (*collectively known as*), and a whole clause

senses.gloss: As a group; all together.
examples: The workers decided *collectively* to go on strike.
These islands are *collectively* known as the Florida Keys.
*Collectively*, the three companies employ over 10,000 people.

senses.gloss: In informal, everyday speech.
examples: The law is *colloquially* known as Obamacare.
In parts of the Midwest, soda is *colloquially* called "pop."
He spoke *colloquially*, as if he were talking to a friend.

senses.gloss: In comfort; in a relaxed way, without pain or money worries.
examples: Are you sitting *comfortably*?
The car seats five people *comfortably*.
They live *comfortably* on her salary.

senses.gloss: Easily, with a clear margin.
senses.ru: уверенно, с запасом, с большим отрывом
examples: She won the race *comfortably*.
The team is *comfortably* ahead in the standings.

senses.gloss: In a way that makes someone feel calmer or less worried.
examples: She patted his hand *comfortingly*.
"It's going to be okay," he said *comfortingly*.
The old house felt *comfortingly* familiar.

position: before its word — before an adjective; also end

senses.gloss: In a funny way, often without meaning to be.
examples: The hat was *comically* large.
He tripped *comically* over his own feet.
The plan was so *comically* bad that no one took it seriously.

position: mid — usually before a participle (*commonly used*)

senses.gloss: Often, usually, or by many people.
examples: Aspirin is *commonly* used to treat headaches.
This mistake is *commonly* made by beginners.
The disease is *more commonly* found in children.

position: end — also before a participle (*communally owned*)

senses.gloss: Shared by or done by a whole group or community.
examples: The land is owned *communally* by the village.
Students cook and eat *communally* in the dorm kitchen.
The garden is managed *communally* by the neighbors.

position: end — also before a participle (*compactly built*)

senses.gloss: In a way that takes up little space; closely and neatly packed.
examples: The tent folds up *compactly* into a small bag.
He was short and *compactly* built, like a wrestler.
If you pack *more compactly*, everything will fit in one suitcase.

position: before its word — before an adjective, participle or adverb

senses.gloss: To a similar degree or in a similar way.
examples: The two phones are *comparably* priced.
Few players performed *comparably* well that season.
No other city in the region has grown at a *comparably* fast pace.

senses.gloss: With sympathy and a wish to help people who are suffering.
examples: The nurse spoke *compassionately* to the grieving family.
We need to treat refugees *compassionately*.
The judge listened *compassionately* but still gave a long sentence.

senses.gloss: Well enough; with the necessary skill.
examples: The job was done *competently*, if not brilliantly.
She handled the crisis *competently*.
He speaks French *competently* but not fluently.

position: before its word — before *priced*; end with verbs of playing

senses.gloss: At a level that can compete with rivals, especially on price.
examples: Their laptops are *competitively* priced.
Small farms can't produce milk *competitively* anymore.

senses.gloss: In organized competitions, not just for fun.
examples: She swam *competitively* in college.
He hasn't played tennis *competitively* in years.

senses.gloss: In a self-satisfied way that ignores possible danger or problems.
examples: He smiled *complacently*, sure he had already won.
We can't sit back *complacently* while prices keep rising.
The team played *complacently* and lost to the worst team in the league.

senses.gloss: Completely, covering everything or nearly everything.
examples: The topic is covered *comprehensively* in chapter three.
The report *comprehensively* reviews the evidence.
The new law *comprehensively* overhauls the tax code.

position: end — also before an adjective (*compulsively readable*)

senses.gloss: Because of a strong urge that is hard to control.
examples: He checks his phone *compulsively*.
She eats *compulsively* when she's stressed.
The novel is *compulsively* readable.

ru: с вычислительной точки зрения, в вычислительном плане
position: before its word — before an adjective (*computationally expensive*); also front

senses.gloss: In terms of the amount of computing it needs.
senses.ru: с вычислительной точки зрения, в вычислительном плане
examples: Training a large model is *computationally* expensive.
The method is simple but *computationally* intensive.
*Computationally*, the problem is much harder than it looks.

position: mid — after a modal (*could conceivably*); also front
modifies: a whole clause, usually with *could* or *might*

senses.gloss: Possibly; in a way that can be imagined or believed.
examples: The trial could *conceivably* last for months.
*Conceivably*, the virus came from bats.
I suppose he might *conceivably* be telling the truth.

position: before its word — before an adjective; also front

senses.gloss: In terms of the basic idea rather than the details.
examples: The idea is *conceptually* simple but hard to build.
*Conceptually*, the two approaches are the same.
The new design is *conceptually* similar to the old one.

senses.gloss: Briefly and clearly, using few words.
examples: Please answer the questions clearly and *concisely*.
She summed up the problem *concisely*.
Try to write *more concisely*.

senses.gloss: In a way that ends all doubt.
examples: The DNA test *conclusively* proved he was innocent.
No one has shown *conclusively* that the drug works.
The question was settled *conclusively* by the Supreme Court.

position: end — also front, introducing a specific example

senses.gloss: In specific, practical terms rather than general ones.
examples: What, *concretely*, are you going to do about it?
*Concretely*, this means hiring three more nurses.
Try to describe the problem *more concretely*.

senses.gloss: At the same time.
examples: The two programs run *concurrently*.
He will serve the two prison sentences *concurrently*.
She worked *concurrently* as a teacher and a translator.

contrast: Russian *снисходительно* can also mean 'leniently, tolerantly' — that is *leniently* or *indulgently*. *Condescendingly* is always an insult: it treats someone as less intelligent or less important.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you think you are smarter or more important than others.
examples: He explained it *condescendingly*, as if I were a child.
She smiled *condescendingly* at the new intern.
Don't talk to me so *condescendingly*.

position: end — also mid, before a participle

senses.gloss: Only if certain conditions are met.
examples: The loan was approved *conditionally*.
He was *conditionally* released from prison.
The college accepted her *conditionally*, pending her final grades.

position: end — front or mid, set off by commas, in the 'between us' sense
contrast: Do not confuse with *confidently* (уверенно). *Confidentially* is about secrecy; *confidently* is about self-assurance.

senses.gloss: In a way that keeps information private or secret.
examples: All applications will be handled *confidentially*.
Employees can talk to a counselor *confidentially*.

senses.gloss: Between you and me; used when telling a secret.
examples: *Confidentially*, I don't think she'll last the year.
He told me, *confidentially*, that the company was for sale.

contrast: Do not confuse with *confidentially* (конфиденциально, по секрету).

senses.gloss: In a sure, self-assured way.
examples: She walked *confidently* into the interview room.
We can *confidently* say the worst is over.
He answered *more confidently* the second time.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; front as a comment
modifies: adjectives, participles, and a whole clause

senses.gloss: In a way that is hard to understand or easy to mix up.
examples: The instructions were *confusingly* written.
*Confusingly*, both brothers are named John.
The two brands have *confusingly* similar logos.

contrast: Do not confuse with *consciously* (сознательно). *Conscientiously* means carefully and dutifully.

senses.gloss: Carefully and thoroughly, trying to do what is right.
examples: She *conscientiously* checked every figure in the report.
He did his homework *conscientiously* every night.
The staff worked *conscientiously* to meet the deadline.

contrast: Do not confuse with *conscientiously* (добросовестно). *Consciously* means knowingly, on purpose.

senses.gloss: Knowingly and on purpose; with awareness.
examples: I wasn't *consciously* trying to copy him.
She *consciously* avoided eye contact.
We are trying to eat *more consciously*.

contrast: Russian *последовательно* also means 'logically, without contradiction' — that is *consistently*. *Consecutively* only means one after another, in order.

senses.gloss: One after another, without a break.
examples: The pages are numbered *consecutively*.
He will serve the sentences *consecutively*, not at the same time.
The prize was awarded to the same team three years *consecutively*.

position: end — before *estimated* in the 'cautious figure' sense; also front

senses.gloss: In a traditional, cautious style that avoids change or risk.
examples: He always dresses *conservatively* for work.
The fund invests its money *conservatively*.

senses.gloss: Cautiously, so that an estimate is probably lower than the real figure.
examples: The damage is *conservatively* estimated at $2 million.
*Conservatively*, the project will take two years.

position: before its word — before a comparative; end with verbs
contrast: Do not confuse with *considerately* (тактично, внимательно к другим). *Considerably* means 'a lot'.

senses.gloss: Much; to a large degree.
examples: The new model is *considerably* cheaper.
Prices have risen *considerably* since last year.
It took *considerably* longer than we expected.

contrast: Do not confuse with *considerably* (значительно). *Considerately* is about thinking of other people.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows care for other people's feelings or needs.
examples: He *considerately* turned the music down so the baby could sleep.
Please park *considerately* and don't block the driveway.
She treated her guests very *considerately*.

senses.gloss: Every time, in the same way, without change or contradiction.
examples: She has *consistently* been the top student in her class.
The restaurant gets *consistently* good reviews.
The rules need to be applied *more consistently*.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*conspicuously absent*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way that is easy to notice, often surprisingly so.
examples: Her name was *conspicuously* absent from the list.
He sat *conspicuously* in the front row.
The mayor has been *conspicuously* silent on the issue.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle

senses.gloss: According to or under a constitution.
examples: Free speech is *constitutionally* protected in the United States.
The court found the law *constitutionally* invalid.

senses.gloss: Because of a person's basic nature or character.
examples: He is *constitutionally* incapable of being on time.
I'm just *constitutionally* unable to sit still.

senses.gloss: In a useful way that helps to improve something.
examples: Let's try to work together *constructively*.
Criticize the work *constructively*, not the person.
She learned to use her anger *constructively*.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you think someone or something is worthless.
examples: She looked *contemptuously* at his old car.
He *contemptuously* tossed the letter aside.
"You call that a plan?" she said *contemptuously*.

senses.gloss: In a happy, satisfied way.
examples: The cat purred *contentedly* on my lap.
He sighed *contentedly* and closed his eyes.
The baby was sleeping *contentedly* in her crib.

senses.gloss: Under the terms of a contract.
examples: The company is *contractually* obligated to finish by June.
Players are *contractually* bound to the team for three years.
We are not *contractually* required to give refunds.

senses.gloss: In a way that causes public disagreement.
examples: *Controversially*, the referee allowed the goal.
The board *controversially* voted to close the library.
The award went, *controversially*, to a first-time author.

position: before its word — before a participle (*conveniently located*); mid in the ironic sense

senses.gloss: In a place or way that is easy and practical.
examples: The hotel is *conveniently* located near the airport.
The store is *conveniently* open until midnight.

senses.gloss: Too neatly for someone's own advantage; used with irony.
examples: He *conveniently* forgot to mention that he was married.
The key evidence *conveniently* disappeared.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle; also end

senses.gloss: In the usual, accepted or traditional way.
examples: She was *conventionally* dressed in a dark suit.
He isn't *conventionally* handsome, but people like him.
The infection is *conventionally* treated with antibiotics.

senses.gloss: In a light, informal way, as in ordinary conversation.
examples: "So, where are you from?" she asked *conversationally*.
The book is *conversationally* written and easy to read.
He mentioned the deal *conversationally*, as if it were nothing.

senses.gloss: In a way that makes people believe something; also, by a clear margin.
examples: She argued *convincingly* for a change in policy.
He lied so *convincingly* that everyone believed him.
The team won *convincingly*, 5 to 0.

contrast: Spelled with double *l*: *coolly*, not *cooly*. It describes manner, never temperature. The two senses pull apart, so the translation depends on context: *received coolly* is холодно, but *coolly walked past the guards* is хладнокровно.

senses.gloss: In an unfriendly or unenthusiastic way.
examples: She greeted him *coolly* and turned away.
The proposal was received *coolly* by the board.

senses.gloss: Calmly, without showing nervousness.
examples: He *coolly* walked past the guards.
She *coolly* sank the winning free throw with one second left.

senses.gloss: By working together toward a shared goal.
examples: The children learned to work *cooperatively* in small groups.
The two agencies acted *cooperatively* to solve the case.
The store is owned and run *cooperatively* by its members.

position: end — also before a participle (*copiously illustrated*)

senses.gloss: In large amounts.
examples: He was bleeding *copiously* from the cut.
She took notes *copiously* during the lecture.
The book is *copiously* illustrated with photos.

senses.gloss: In a warm, friendly but polite way.
examples: You are *cordially* invited to our wedding.
The ambassador was received *cordially* at the White House.
The two leaders *cordially* shook hands.

contrast: Russian *корректно* usually means 'politely, properly' — that is *politely* or *appropriately*. *Correctly* means 'without mistakes'.

senses.gloss: Without mistakes; in the right way.
examples: Did I pronounce your name *correctly*?
She answered all the questions *correctly*.
If I remember *correctly*, the store closes at nine.

position: before its word — before an adjective or comparative; also end or front
modifies: adjectives, comparatives, verbs, and a whole clause
contrast: Russian *соответственно* has three English equivalents: 'to a matching degree' is *correspondingly*; 'so, therefore' is *so* or *accordingly*; 'in the order given' is *respectively*.

senses.gloss: To a matching degree; in a way that matches something just mentioned.
examples: The job is harder, and the pay is *correspondingly* higher.
Demand fell, and prices dropped *correspondingly*.
The risks are greater, and the rewards are *correspondingly* large.

senses.gloss: Dishonestly, by abusing power, usually for money.
examples: The judge was accused of acting *corruptly*.
Officials *corruptly* awarded the contract to a friend's company.
The city had been run *corruptly* for decades.

position: before its word — before an adjective or participle

senses.gloss: In appearance only, not in how something works or what it is.
examples: The car was only *cosmetically* damaged.
The new version is only *cosmetically* different from the old one.
The house looks great *cosmetically*, but the roof still leaks.

form: flat — the same form as the adjective *counter*
contrast: The same spelling is a noun (*the kitchen counter*) and a verb (*to counter an argument*). As an adverb it comes almost only in *run counter to* and *go counter to*.

senses.gloss: In the opposite direction to something; against it.
examples: The decision runs *counter* to everything we believe in.
These results go *counter* to earlier research.
Acting *counter* to your doctor's advice is risky.

position: front — also mid, set off by commas

senses.gloss: In a way that is the opposite of what you would expect.
senses.ru: вопреки ожиданиям, как ни странно, парадоксально
examples: *Counterintuitively*, closing a lane made traffic move faster.
The more choices people have, *counterintuitively*, the less happy they are.
Adding more staff *counterintuitively* slowed the project down.

senses.gloss: With courage; bravely.
examples: She fought her illness *courageously*.
The firefighters acted *courageously* to save the children.
He spoke out *courageously* against corruption.
